meta.scope: I-90 EB from the Mount Baker Ridge Tunnel over the Lacey V. Murrow floating bridge, Mercer Island and the East Channel Bridge, I-405 NB to downtown Bellevue (NE 8th St, Bellevue Way, 108th Ave NE, Lincoln Square, Bellevue Square, Plaza Center).
meta.units: metres unless suffixed (_in, _ft); lat/lon WGS84; colours sRGB hex
meta.howToUse: chapterRoutes[].segments are OSM ways in driving order with lane/turn/destination tags; streets[] = curated corridor stretches + downtown catalogue; buildings[] = every building within 70 m of a route or ≥25 m tall in the core, with OSM parts + curated heights/facades; landmarks[] has lincoln-square and plaza-center (CV stops); traffic.hotspots feed CITIES.seattle.districts.bellevue.congestion.

sourceRoofReview.source: Explicit original OSM roof/carport classification; all source footprints inspected in independent Esri aerial context
sourceRoofReview.dimensionStatus: Unsourced vertical bands and supports remain estimates. Literal source height/min_height wins; layer is never a metre height. Legal maxheight is only a lower bound on clear underside.

district.name: Lake Washington & Bellevue
district.proposal: Corridor district (not a 1 km square): the I-90 crossing is the chapter's point. Keep (1) a 250 m-wide band either side of I-90 from the Mount Baker Tunnel west lid portal (lon -122.3030) to the I-90/I-405 interchange (lon -122.1820), including the lake surface to the horizon as a non-driveable plane with both shorelines as backdrop; (2) a 200 m band around I-405 from I-90 (lat 47.578) to NE 10th St (lat 47.6195); (3) the downtown core 1 km² box Main St → NE 12th St × 100th Ave NE → I-405; (4) for route B, a 120 m band along Bellevue Way SE/NE.

endOfMap.where: I-90 WB/EB west of the Mount Baker lid (lon -122.3030)
endOfMap.how: tunnel lid interior: fade-to-dark + "ROAD CLOSED" barricade inside the WB tunnel; EB traffic spawns from darkness
Type III barricade + "END OF MAP" on the 16-lane section; real cue: the disused BNSF Wilburton-area railroad bridge over I-90 (src wp-i90) makes a natural visual cut

endOfMap.where: I-405 south of I-90 / north of NE 10th
endOfMap.how: construction-zone closure (plausible: Renton–Bellevue ETL work zone is real through 2027, src wsdot-r2b)
ramps end at the signal at the top with a barricade; island streets not modelled beyond 80 m

scenicNotes: On the Murrow bridge the downtown Bellevue skyline is dead ahead/left, Mount Rainier to the right (SSE) on clear days, Seattle skyline in the mirror (src commons).
Lake surface ~ at deck level minus 2-3 m (floating pontoons): no bridge piers on the floating section.

chapterRoutes.title: Spec route: Mount Baker Tunnel → Murrow floating bridge → Mercer Island lids → East Channel Bridge → I-405 N → exit 13B NE 8th St W → Plaza Center

start.note: Inside the south 1940 Mount Baker Ridge Tunnel bore (EB, 2 GP lanes), ~150 m before the east portal: the chapter opens with the bright portal and the lake ahead. Spawn in the right lane (lane 2 of 2).

stop.note: Plaza Center, 10900 NE 8th St, in front of the tower on the NE 8th St westbound carriageway.

chapterRoutes.timing: ≈ 9.5 min at the 60 mph limit off-peak; I-405 NB through downtown is a weekday AM/PM hotspot (see traffic).
chapterRoutes.warning: Longer than spec 10 acceptance (bellevue ≤ 12 km): 14.4 km. To fit 12 km, start on the Murrow bridge just past the west high-rise (s≈2.0 km) — loses the tunnel portal moment — or accept 14.4 km for the finale.

chapterRoutes.title: Scenic alternative: same lake crossing → I-90 exit 9 Bellevue Way → Bellevue Way SE (Enatai, Mercer Slough, Surrey Downs) → Old Bellevue / Main St → Bellevue Way NE past Downtown Park, Bellevue Square, Lincoln Square → right on NE 8th St → Plaza Center

stop.side: south kerb of NE 8th EB; Plaza Center is across the street (north side)

chapterRoutes.timing: ≈ 13 min off-peak (30 mph arterials, ~13 signals on Bellevue Way)
chapterRoutes.note: 13.2 km. Passes every downtown hero landmark (Lincoln Square, Bellevue Square, skybridges, Bellevue Collection) at street level; does not use I-405. Could also end at Lincoln Square (2025 office) instead of Plaza Center (2022 office).

streets.name: I-90 EB — Mount Baker Ridge Tunnel (1940 twin bores + 1990s lid)
streets.lengthM: lid+tunnel ≈ 1,000 m perceived (official tunnel 1,440 ft/440 m + 2,000 ft lid)
streets.lanes: West of tunnel 4 EB lanes (left = HOV 2+, 3 GP). Inside, at lon -122.2986, splits into the two 1940 bores: NORTH bore = HOV lane + GP lane (way 123889282, hov:lanes designated|), SOUTH bore = 2 GP lanes (98733141/481403971). Each bore 2 lanes; bores rejoin into 4 lanes on the Murrow bridge approach (way 123889285).
streets.geometry: Original bores 29 ft (8.8 m) diameter; after 1989–93 rehab the interiors were made square/rectangular (except the arched portal openings). Westbound + the former reversible lanes use the separate 63 ft (19 m) 1989 bore to the north, double-decked with the I-90 Trail on top.
streets.portals: East portals (EB exits here): 1940 art-deco concrete arches with relief panels and the inscription "SEATTLE · PORTAL TO THE PACIFIC" — the "Portal of the North Pacific" murals by James FitzGerald; City of Seattle landmark (src wp-mtbaker, commons Seattle_-_Portal_to_the_Pacific_01.jpg). Concrete #b9b6ad weathered, vegetation on the slope above, the round mouth of the 1989 bore to the north.
streets.interior: Rectangular box, light-grey concrete walls; continuous linear luminaires on the ceiling edges; WSDOT lane-control signals absent on EB (only on the former reversible bore). Lighting: warm/orange-ish tint visible in photos at the portal (src commons).
streets.markings: White 4 in dashed lane line 10/30 ft between the 2 lanes of each bore; solid white right edge, solid yellow left edge (one-way roadway rule, src wsdot-m2010 note 2); HOV diamond in the north-bore left lane.
streets.barriers: Tunnel walls form the edges; no shoulders inside the 1940 bores (narrow ~0.6 m curbs/walkways).

streets.name: I-90 EB — Lacey V. Murrow Memorial Bridge (floating, 1940/1993)
facts: Carries 4 EB lanes; second-longest floating bridge in the world, 6,620 ft (2,020 m); original opened 1940, sank 1990 during rehab, current bridge opened 1993.
Boats pass only under elevated fixed spans at each end (29 ft clearance) — the "west high-rise" and "east high-rise".
streets.lanes: 4 EB: lane 1 (left) HOV 2+ (bus designated) + 3 GP. At the east end the right lane becomes exit 6 West Mercer Way (destination:lanes none|none|none|none;West Mercer Way).
streets.surface: portland-cement concrete deck, light grey #8e8f8a dry / #5f615e wet (photo median #787974 in low winter sun)
streets.structure: Both ends: the iconic cream concrete "high-rise" through-arches — a pair of parabolic arch ribs per end whose tops join in a flattened oval ring with round lightening holes, vertical dark steel hangers (~8 per side per arch) holding the deck; the deck rises ~9 m over the navigation channel then drops to the floating section. Arch concrete #c9c0ae (photo #b8a68b in warm sun). Floating section: deck sits ~2–3 m above the water on concrete pontoons (grey), joined by expansion joints with steel finger plates every pontoon (~110 m).
streets.barriers: Low concrete safety-shape (F-shape/jersey) parapets ~0.8 m both sides, dark-stained grey #3a3a38 on the outside face; no sidewalk on the Murrow (pedestrians/bikes use the Hadley trail). Light poles on the parapet line, single davit arms.
streets.markings: Dashed white lane lines (4 in, 10 ft dash/30 ft gap) supplemented by raised pavement markers between dashes; solid yellow left edge line next to the narrow left shoulder; solid white right edge line; wide (8 in) lane line between HOV and GP lanes; white diamond in lane 1 at intervals.
streets.view: Mercer Island ahead with houses on the wooded bluff, the Hadley bridge 20–40 m to the left (north) with WB traffic and 2 Line trains under catenary in its centre roadway, downtown Bellevue towers half-left, Mt Rainier right on clear days.

streets.name: I-90 WB — Homer M. Hadley Memorial Bridge (floating, 1989) — the opposite carriageway, visible to the north
cross-section (north→south): I-90 Trail (multi-use path, concrete, ~3.5 m) with black steel picket railing on a concrete parapet
WB roadway: 4 lanes (HOV left + 3 GP), shoulders

centre roadway: 2 Line light-rail double track on the former reversible express roadway, overhead catenary on portal frames (dark grey steel), opened for passenger service across the lake on 2026-03-28 — world's first light rail on a floating bridge
streets.pontoons: 18 pontoons, 105 ft (32 m) wide incl. cantilevers.
streets.note: Model it: the player sees it constantly for 2 km. WB traffic is heavy 15:30–18:30 (85% of weekdays severely congested at 16:35, src wsdot-dash-90).

streets.name: I-90 EB across Mercer Island (Mercer Island/First Hill lid, downtown MI, Luther Burbank lid)
streets.lanes: 4 EB (HOV + 3 GP) throughout; exits 7A 77th Ave SE, 7B Island Crest Way (right), 8 East Mercer Way (right, destination:lanes ...;East Mercer Way). HOV direct-access ramp to Island Crest Way/80th from the left lane (motor_vehicle=no, bus+HOV only).
streets.tunnels: EB passes through short covered sections: the "I-90 First Hill Lid" (way 4744334, 788 m, lit) under the Aubrey Davis Park lid, plus several 40–50 m lid/overpass undercrossings (layer -1) near 76th–80th Ave SE, and a "covered" section at Luther Burbank (lon -122.213).
streets.median: Mercer Island light-rail station (2 Line) sits in the I-90 median between 77th and 80th Ave SE (opened 2026-03-28 with the cross-lake segment); tracks run in the centre roadway between EB and WB with concrete barriers both sides.
streets.walls: Tall concrete retaining walls and noise walls (OSM wall=noise_barrier near 76th–80th) line the cut; vegetated slopes; lid park above.

streets.name: I-90 EB — East Channel Bridge (fixed, to Bellevue)
streets.lanes: 4 → 5 EB: an added right lane drops to exit 9 Bellevue Way; on the bridge destination:lanes "Everett;Renton;none | none | none | none | none;Bellevue Way" — the LEFT HOV lane carries the direct HOV ramp to I-405 (and to Bellevue Way via the HOV-only slip at way 1013755121).
streets.structure: Concrete box-girder fixed bridge high over the East Channel of Lake Washington, concrete parapets, Enatai/Beaux Arts shoreline houses below to the north-east.

streets.name: I-90 EB exit 10A "I-405 N Everett" (flyover) → I-405 NB
streets.lanes: I-90 5 lanes at the split: lanes 4–5 exit (lane 4 "Factoria Blvd; Everett", lane 5 "Renton"); ramp 2 lanes → 3 lanes → splits (left "Everett"/I-405 N, right "Renton"/I-405 S) → single-lane flyover (layer 2) curving north over I-90 and the Mercer Slough → merges into I-405 NB from the right.
streets.structure: Elevated concrete flyovers of the I-90/I-405 stack (layer 1–2), concrete jersey parapets, tall single-arm light poles.

streets.name: I-405 NB — I-90 to exit 13 (NE 4th / NE 8th)
streets.lanes: 5 NB south of SE 8th (HOV 2+ left + 4 GP) → 4 after exit 12 (SE 8th St) → 5 at the exit-13 auxiliary lane: destination:lanes "none|none|Seattle|Redmond;NE 4th St|NE 8th St" (lanes 3–4 continue to SR 520 Seattle/Redmond, lane 5 exits).
streets.surface: concrete south of NE 4th, asphalt overlays near downtown (OSM surface tags)
streets.context: Ten lanes total through Bellevue; passes the Mercer Slough and the historic Wilburton Trestle; the 2 Line guideway crosses overhead near NE 6th (src wp-i405). Renton–Bellevue widening (dual express toll lanes) is UNDER CONSTRUCTION, forecast opening summer 2027 (src wsdot-r2b): in Nov 2026 expect work-zone barrels, temporary concrete barriers and orange signs on the stretch near I-90/SE 8th.
streets.median: Concrete median barrier between NB and SB (profile/glare screen not verified); HOV lane on the left separated by a wide broken white line with diamonds; narrow left shoulder with yellow edge line.

streets.name: Exit 13B ramp → "NE 8th St West" loop → NE 8th St WB
streets.lanes: 2-lane exit (13A left to NE 4th "Meydenbauer Center / Bellevue Square / Bellevue Arts Museum", 13B right to NE 8th) → 13B splits "NE 8th St East" / "NE 8th St West"; the West ramp is a 1-lane braided/loop ramp entering NE 8th WB from the right at 112th Ave NE.
streets.note: The NE 6th St "Texas T" HOV/transit direct-access ramp leaves I-405 from the LEFT lane just north of exit 13 — HOV/buses only; do not route the player there.

streets.name: Bellevue Way SE (route B) — I-90 exit 9 to Main St
streets.lanes: 2–3 lanes, partly one-way pairs at the I-90 ramps, HOV lane NB south of 112th Ave SE (OSM hov:lanes), then 4–5 lanes with centre turn lane through Enatai / Surrey Downs to Main St.
streets.context: Passes South Bellevue station/park-and-ride (2 Line), Mercer Slough Nature Park (wetland, blueberry farms), Winters House; 30 mph; WSDOT/Bellevue signals at SE 30th, 112th Ave SE, SE 16th.
streets.congestion: PM peak southbound toward I-90 is the slow direction: 2019 PM travel time 112th Ave SE → I-90 2.38 min SB vs 1.82 NB (src bel-mip2).

streets.name: NE 8th Street (downtown, 112th Ave NE → Bellevue Way NE)
streets.lanes: Principal arterial, 30 mph. Mapped as two one-way carriageways ~11–14 m apart centre-to-centre → 3–4 lanes per direction incl. left-turn pockets (turn:lanes "left|||right" WB at 106th/108th) with a narrow raised median between. 7 lanes total typical mid-block.
streets.surface: asphalt #3d3f42 (patched, darker fresh overlays); concrete crosswalk aprons at some corners
streets.sidewalk: Downtown standard DT-120-1: concrete, 2 ft × 2 ft scored squares, light broom finish; ≥5 ft planter/tree strip at the kerb (src bel-tdm). Kerb: 6 in vertical concrete with gutter.
streets.signals: Signalised at 112th, 110th, 108th, 106th Ave NE and Bellevue Way; mast-arm poles with 12-in 3-section heads with retroreflective backplates, one per lane, street-name sign on each arm (src bel-tdm 4.1.2–4.1.6).
streets.congestion: PM peak v/c 1.00 at 112th Ave NE (2018 count) — the worst downtown intersection on this street; 0.66 at 108th, 0.66 at Bellevue Way (src bel-mip2).

streets.name: Bellevue Way NE (Main St → NE 8th St, route B)
streets.lanes: 30 mph; mapped as split carriageways (centre spacing 9.7–12.3 m) with 2–3 lanes each way + left-turn pockets at NE 2nd, NE 4th, NE 6th (Lincoln Square South/Bellevue Square entrance), NE 8th.
streets.frontage: West side: Bellevue Square mall (Nordstrom, Macy's, Cheesecake Factory, Shake Shack…), Bellevue Downtown Park further south. East side: Lincoln Square South podium (Fogo de Chão, Duke's, Wild Ginger), Lincoln Square North (Earls, Din Tai Fung, Paddy Coyne's). Covered skybridge over Bellevue Way at ~NE 7th (2007, src wp-bsq).
streets.congestion: PM v/c: Main St 0.93, NE 4th 0.59, NE 8th 0.66, NE 12th 0.71 (src bel-mip2).

facade.description: Storefront glazing at grade, warm stone/precast and brick-red masonry panels above (photo #b57f52 for the brick-toned masonry seen from Downtown Park), canopies over the Bellevue Way sidewalk.

landmarks.name: Plaza Center — UiPath Bellevue 2018–2025 (10900 NE 8th St, Suite 400)
landmarks.note: Briefly Bellevue's tallest building (1982–83). Part of "The Plaza Buildings" with Plaza East (11100 NE 8th, 9 fl, OSM 33725872) — Kilroy/KORE-managed office pair.
landmarks.footprint: rectangle ≈ 60 m (N-S) × 35 m (E-W) with chamfered/notched corners (OSM ring), long axis perpendicular to NE 8th; north side of NE 8th between 108th and 110th Ave NE, set back ~20 m behind a plaza.

entrance.faces: south, onto NE 8th St (glazed lobby under the "10900" letters)
entrance.confidence: medium — photo shows the main doors on the NE 8th frontage; no OSM entrance node

facade.description: Classic 1982 vertical-stripe tower: full-height ivory/cream precast piers alternating with continuous dark bronze-charcoal glass strips (~0.9 m pier / ~1.2 m glass rhythm, ~13 bays on the long face), notched/chamfered corners with a glass strip on each chamfer, flat roof behind a plain ivory parapet band. Small dark "PLAZA CENTER" letters near the top of the east face. Ground floor: recessed black-glazed podium with "10900" address letters over the entrance and a U.S. Bank branch (red/white logo; OSM node 697212592). At the west driveway a tall black pylon with huge vertical white numerals "10900".

landmarks.street: In front: NE 8th St WB lanes, raised median whose kerb noses are painted yellow, white dashed lane lines with raised markers; young street trees in planters (autumn colour orange/red in late Oct).

landmarks.name: Mount Baker Ridge Tunnel east portals ("Seattle · Portal to the Pacific")
landmarks.description: Twin 1940 arched concrete portals with low-relief art-deco/Northwest-native murals and the carved inscription "SEATTLE PORTAL TO THE PACIFIC"; above-left the huge round mouth of the 1989 bore (WB + trail). City of Seattle landmark with the Murrow bridge.

landmarks.name: Lacey V. Murrow bridge "high-rise" arch spans (west & east ends)
landmarks.description: Two cream-white concrete through-arches per end that the EB lanes drive through: arch ribs lean in and fuse into a flattened elliptical crown ring with a row of oval holes; ~8 dark vertical steel hangers per side per arch. Colour #c9c0ae (sunlit photo #b8a68b).

landmarks.name: Lacey V. Murrow Memorial Bridge dedication plaque (1967)
landmarks.text: LACEY V. MURROW MEMORIAL BRIDGE — UNIQUE, FUNCTIONAL AND BEAUTIFUL, THIS FLOATING BRIDGE IS HEREBY DEDICATED TO THE MEMORY OF MR. LACEY V. MURROW, DYNAMIC DIRECTOR OF HIGHWAYS, A BRIGADIER GENERAL IN THE U.S. AIR FORCE, AND INTERNATIONALLY KNOWN CONSULTING ENGINEER. JUNE 30, 1967 — WASHINGTON STATE HIGHWAY COMMISSION
landmarks.note: At the East Portal Viewpoint above the tunnel (not visible from the road).

Slender twin glass towers with blue-green glazing and white horizontal slab edges; rooftop garden between them.

markings.standardsNote: Washington State uses the federal MUTCD with WSDOT Standard Plans; Bellevue arterials follow MUTCD + WSDOT plans (src bel-tdm intro).

laneLine.pattern: 10 ft dash / 30 ft gap (3.05 m / 9.14 m)

wideBrokenLaneLine.use: HOV-to-GP separation on contiguous HOV lanes (MUTCD 3D.02: wide broken white where crossing is permitted)

dottedLaneLine.use: lane drops / auxiliary lanes / through interchange (e.g., exit-only lanes on I-405 NB at exit 13)

dottedExtension.pattern: 2 ft / 6 ft; wide version 8 in 6 ft / 6 ft (gore & ramp extensions)

edgeLines.left: solid yellow on one-way roadways (all freeway carriageways, one-way couplets)

doubleCenterline.spacing_in: 12 in on state routes; 4 in at left-turn channelisation, narrow (≤10 ft lane) roads and optionally on local streets (Bellevue)

markings.twoWayLeftTurn: yellow solid outer + yellow broken (10/30) inner lines, with white TWLTL arrows
markings.material: Profiled plastic (raised bumps every 2 ft on 4 in lines) and embossed plastic lines on WSDOT freeways — gives the textured, rain-visible look (src wsdot-m2020); MMA profiled bumps in western WA (src columbian-2024).

raisedPavementMarkers.standard: Type 2W (white, one-way reflective face) centred in each 30 ft gap of lane lines at 80 ft intervals on tangents/curves ≥1500 ft radius, 40 ft on tighter curves; Type 2Y (yellow, one side) outside the left edge line every 80 ft; Type 2YY on two-way centrelines (src wsdot-m2030).
raisedPavementMarkers.boTTsDots: Western Washington historically used Type 1 non-reflective ceramic buttons (Botts' dots) to SIMULATE lane lines on many highways and arterials (src wsdot-m5102); on I-90/I-405 today expect painted/profiled lines + Type 2 reflective RPMs; Bellevue arterials: painted lines, some legacy button lines on older streets.
raisedPavementMarkers.size: Type 2 RPM ≈ 4 in × 4 in × 0.7 in prismatic; Type 1 Botts dot 4 in diameter, 0.75 in domed, white ceramic

hovDiamond.min: 2.5 ft wide × 12 ft long, lines ≥ 6 in (MUTCD); WSDOT freeway diamonds are ~12–16 ft long
hovDiamond.spacing: freeway: up to ~1,000 ft and at decision points; city streets as close as 80 ft

markings.gores: Gore areas: 8 in wide solid white channelising lines with white chevrons (crosshatch) 12 in wide at ≥45 mph, 8 in at ≤40 mph (M-24.60 crosshatch); ramp exits begin with wide dotted lines, then solid wide line at the gore (src wsdot-m2460, wsdot-m2010).
markings.stopLines: 12–24 in white solid ("1'-6" unless noted") (src wsdot-m2460)
markings.crosswalks: Downtown Bellevue: white continental (ladder) crosswalks at signals; some textured/coloured; diagonal "scramble" at Bellevue Transit Center (NE 6th × 108th/110th) (src commons file "Bellevue Transit Center Scramble").
markings.bikeLanes: 6 in solid white line + bike symbol; green paint at conflict zones on 108th Ave NE (OSM cycleway tags) — verify
markings.onBridges: Murrow/Hadley: same freeway pattern; expansion-joint steel plates cross the markings every pontoon joint.

signals.poles: Bellevue standard Type II/III mast-arm poles (single arm per approach), terminal cabinet facing away from the intersection; one 12-in 3-section head per lane over the arm (WSDOT J-75.20 Type M mounting), backplates with retroreflective border, signs: street-name blade at the far right of each arm; emergency pre-emption detector on each arm (src bel-tdm).
signals.colour: galvanised/grey steel poles typical; some downtown poles painted dark (verify per intersection)
signals.pedestrian: countdown pedestrian heads + accessible push buttons (MUTCD)

streetLights.freeway: single davit/bent-arm aluminium poles ~40 ft with LED cobra heads on the median/parapet line (OSM lamp_mount=bent_mast ×74 in district)
streetLights.downtown: roadway pole with LED fixture per Bellevue Street Lighting Design Guide 2024; pedestrian-scale decorative poles in Old Bellevue (Main St)

furniture.freewayBarriers: Concrete safety-shape median barriers (single-slope ~42–50 in on I-405), F-shape parapets on the floating bridges and flyovers; W-beam guardrail on some ramp edges; OSM barrier=jersey_barrier ×19 in the I-90 corridor; noise walls (wall=noise_barrier) on Mercer Island and near the Mount Baker lid.
furniture.gantries: Sign bridges are galvanised steel box trusses spanning the carriageway (OSM man_made=gantry; 30+ in district), signs green with white legend, exit tabs on top-left/right, yellow "EXIT ONLY" panels at the bottom of lane-drop signs.
furniture.sidewalks: Downtown: concrete DT-120-1, 2×2 ft scoring, light broom finish, ≥5 ft planter strip with street trees/lights between kerb and walk; 12-in step-off where parking (src bel-tdm). Kerb 6 in vertical concrete, gutter pan 2 ft.
furniture.busStops: King County Metro: blue/white "Metro" flag on a pole, shelters glass with dark frames; RapidRide B Line stations with red/yellow pylon (src commons RapidRide photos, osm).
furniture.other: Fire hydrants (OSM emergency=fire_hydrant ×49 downtown; body colour not verified), Big Belly-style bins, benches in planters, public art (OSM tourism=artwork ×45 downtown), parking-garage entrances (OSM amenity=parking_entrance ×113).

lightRail.vehicles: Siemens S70/S700 LRVs, white body, Sound Transit blue lower band with teal/green wave graphics, "Link" logo; 2–4 car trains; overhead catenary on steel portal frames (src commons 2026 photos, wp-2line)

kcm: RapidRide B Line (#96172E red/yellow livery) on NE 8th / 112th
bus.liveries: King County Metro: white/yellow/teal ("Metro" 2020s) or legacy white-blue; RapidRide: red/yellow/grey with "RapidRide" on side; Sound Transit Express: white with blue/teal swoosh, ST logo

colours.note: Photo-derived values are medians of hand-picked regions in refs/bellevue photos (scripts in md); adjust for lighting — sunny photos skew warm.

hotspots.direction: I-405 NB (Tukwila/Renton → Bellevue) through SE 8th → NE 8th
hotspots.evidence: Corridor congested up to 15 h/day; 192,000 ADT at NE 8th/NE 4th (src wsdot-css504). Bellevue→Everett NB severe congestion at 16:25 on 70% of 2024 weekdays (src wsdot-dash-405). Renton–Bellevue construction zone through 2027 adds backups (src wsdot-r2b, wsdot-r2b-news-2026).
Bellevue→Tukwila at ~17:00 below 36 mph on up to 97% of days (2014); Everett→Bellevue SB 07:30 severe on 73% of 2024 weekdays.

hotspots.direction: I-90 WB (Bellevue → Seattle) on the Hadley bridge — OPPOSITE carriageway, visible beside the player
hotspots.evidence: Bellevue→Seattle severe congestion at 08:25 on 54.8% and at 16:35 on 84.6% of 2024 weekdays (src wsdot-dash-90).
Seattle→Bellevue severe at 17:10 on only 20.9% of 2024 weekdays — mostly flowing (src wsdot-dash-90).

hotspots.direction: NE 8th St at 112th Ave NE / I-405 ramps
hotspots.evidence: PM peak v/c 1.00 (2018), forecast 1.31 (2044) — the most saturated downtown intersection on the route (src bel-mip2).

hotspots.direction: Bellevue Way SE southbound to I-90 (route B opposite direction)
hotspots.evidence: 2019 PM SB travel time 2.38 min vs 1.82 NB for 112th Ave SE→I-90 (src bel-mip2).

hotspots.direction: Bellevue Way NE at Bellevue Square/Lincoln Square garages
hotspots.evidence: Retail peak (23 M annual visitors, src wp-bsq); holiday season Nov–Dec heavier. Estimated, no counts found.

traffic.regional: Seattle 7th most congested US city in TomTom 2025, ~66–69 h lost/yr, peak ~17:00, summer worst (src tomtom-sea).

speedLimits.ramps: advisory 30–40 mph yellow plaques on loops
speedLimits.downtown arterials: 30 mph (OSM maxspeed on NE 8th, Bellevue Way, 108th…)
